Roman Empire goes to war with Sasanian Persia; Galerius is initially defeated
The Xianbei Yuwen tribe defeats the Murong tribe; Murong Gui flees to Liaodong
A great fire breaks out in the Luoyang arsenal, burning a huge quantity of weapons and armor
Roman Caesar Galerius regroups his forces on the Persian frontier, preparing a counterattack
The Di tribal leader Qi Wannian rises in Guanzhong and proclaims himself emperor
Drought in Guanzhong leads to a large influx of refugees into Shu, causing social unrest
Roman Caesar Galerius attacks Persia again, initially defeated but then wins a great victory
The Jin general Zhou Chu fights at the Battle of Liuwu without support and dies in combat
Diocletian issues the Edict on Maximum Prices, fixing maximum prices for goods and services
Famine continues in Guanzhong; Li Te leads refugees into Shu to seek food
Roman Caesar Galerius defeats the Sasanian Persian king Narseh in Armenia
Jin general Meng Guan leads elite troops to suppress Qi Wannian's rebellion, killing Qi Wannian
Diocletian's Edict on Maximum Prices has little effect
Rome and Sasanian Persia sign a peace treaty, maintaining peace for nearly forty years
Empress Jia deposes the crown prince Sima Yu, provoking widespread anger
Maya civilization enters the Classic period
Ghana Empire rises
The Pandya kingdom peaks
